note: File: S3 r4/modal_t3-01/t3/T3.jsonl (500 rows, one per problem_index), fetched to runs/theory-tests/r4/modal_t3-01/t3/T3.jsonl. Grader v3 = rln4_lib.grade_v3 (the function rln4_grader_v3.py calls); v3_last is recomputed from text and gold. Self-opened = '\nOkay' in text[:60]. First marker = the earliest of the first line whose lstrip begins 'Answer:' (position taken at 'Answer:') and the first '\boxed{' (brace-balanced, else the rest of the text). first_score = grade_v3(gold, 'Answer: ' + content). Read literally, v3 re-extracts from that string: it uses only the first line of a multi-line content, prefers any \boxed inside the content, and gives 0 to empty content. alt_measured grades the stripped content directly (S.grade(norm_v3(gold), norm_v3(content))) with no re-extraction. Empty-text rows count as v3_last 0 with no marker, so they sit in the denominator with first_score 0. The bootstrap resamples the filtered rows. 'Report nothing' with an empty filter becomes not_computable. example_row text is cut to 2,000 characters.

Same file, filters, marker and grading as k=1, on all non-self-opened first rows with cap hits included. Discordant = first_score != v3_last; statistic = share of discordant rows with first_score == 1. alt_measured uses the k=1 alternative first_score (content graded directly), so its discordant set is recomputed and can differ. The bootstrap resamples the discordant rows only. No discordant rows -> not_computable ('report nothing').

Same file and self-opened rule. Kept: cap_hit False and grade_v3 score 0 on the full text. End of an 'Answer:' marker = the '\n' that ends its line (the remainder starts with that newline). End of a box = just after its matching '}' (end of text if unbalanced). Run-on = a marker exists AND len(text[end:]) > 300 AND (the remainder contains '\boxed{' OR some line of the full text starting at or after end has lstrip starting 'Answer:'). Ambiguity: 'another line' in the remainder. The main reading uses whole lines of the text, so the tail of a box's own line does not count. alt_measured splits the remainder on '\n', so that tail also counts if it begins 'Answer:'. Kept rows with no marker count as not run-on.

File: S3 r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl (500 rows, one per problem_index), fetched to runs/theory-tests/r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl. The file has no score_v3 field, so the score is recomputed with rln4_lib.grade_v3(gold, text); cap hits are kept. M = 'Wait' in text or 'Hmm' in text (case-sensitive substrings, so 'Hmmm' also matches). Only the text field is searched: the cue/opener prefix is not prepended, and if text holds the generation without the opener, an opener containing these words would be missed. The recipe is unambiguous, so alt_measured is a sensitivity reading: the same difference with cap-hit rows excluded. The bootstrap resamples problems. A resample with an empty group returns 0.0 (unlikely at n=500, but it could narrow the interval if M is tiny). An empty group in the real data -> not_computable.

Bootstrap and empty-group handling are as in k=4. example_row drops the prompt field and cuts text to 2,000 characters.
